body.x: Awesome Lab Co., Ltd. (CEO Martin Kim) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Awesome Lab is a startup developing electric hot water and heating solutions based on electrolysis ionization heat-generation technology. Since developing the core technology in 2022, the company has secured domestic and international patents and certifications and increased brand recognition through its B2C-focused ‘WATERWARMER’ brand.

Building on WATERWARMER, Awesome Lab confirmed overseas demand by raising 5,100% of its funding target through a crowdfunding campaign in Japan. The company has also been steadily expanding its business scope and markets by supplying hybrid heating solutions to commercial and residential facilities, smart farms, smart cities, and manufacturing sites.

At CES 2026, Awesome Lab showcased its hot water and heating solution, ‘Thermoflux.’ Thermoflux operates by using ionization reactions that occur during the electrical activation of water, generating heat directly from the water itself without separate heaters or combustion.

Unlike the indirect heating structure of conventional electric boilers, this heat-generation method enables simultaneous heat production and fluid circulation, reducing heat loss while increasing heat transfer efficiency. According to the company, under the same hot water and heating output conditions, Thermoflux maintains 20–30% lower power consumption than conventional electric heating systems, while also offering fast heating response and stable, continuous operation.

In addition, Thermoflux delivers heating speeds up to twice as fast as typical electric boilers and achieves carbon emission reductions of approximately 25–80%. Awesome Lab also emphasized that the system reduces installation space by up to 30% and maximizes installation and maintenance efficiency through a modular design approach.

Thermoflux further operates based on proprietary electrode design and current-control technologies, enabling precise suppression of overheating and structurally reducing safety risks, such as fire hazards, often associated with high-temperature heaters or gas combustion equipment.

At CES 2026, Thermoflux was introduced as a heat-source technology applicable not only to domestic hot water and heating but also to a wide range of industrial environments that require continuous heat supply. As an electric system with no combustion process, it drew attention as an effective alternative to conventional hot water and heating systems amid tightening global regulations on gas boilers and decarbonization policies.

An Awesome Lab representative said, “We were pleased to confirm global market interest in our next-generation hot water and heating solution at CES,” adding, “We received positive feedback by presenting objective data on tangible benefits such as improved heating response and carbon reduction, and by clearly highlighting Thermoflux’s advantages through comparisons with existing boiler systems.”

The representative continued, “Through the networks gained at this exhibition, our goal is to solidify partnerships for overseas pilots and commercialization and to open sales channels in markets around the world,” adding, “Having already accumulated meaningful data and references through PoC projects in Japan, the United States, and Mongolia, we view the potential to attract new customers and partners very positively.”
